featured_reviews.name: Gajanan Padhi
featured_reviews.review_text:
One of the most authentic South Indian breakfast experiences in Thane.

I recently visited Benne Rush for a food-blogging shoot, and honestly, this place completely exceeded expectations. Their Benne Dosa is made using pure Nandini ghee and butter, following the traditional benne technique, which gives it that beautiful golden crisp with a rich, aromatic finish.

The highlight for me was their Madras Onion Podi Uttapam — made with small Madras onions, perfectly crisp on the edges, soft inside, and bursting with bold South Indian flavours. You won’t find this combination done this well anywhere else in Thane.

Their Ghee Podi Thatte Idli was soft, fluffy, and generously loaded with hot ghee and spicy podi — pure comfort food. And the Kumbakonam filter coffee was absolutely spot-on: strong, aromatic, and brewed the traditional way.

What really sets Benne Rush apart is their commitment to freshness — their chutneys are made fresh every 3 hours, which makes a huge difference in taste and quality.

If you love real South Indian food, this place is a must-visit. Highly recommended for dosa lovers and breakfast enthusiasts.

This place is run by a Tamilian family. Serves freshly made south indian tiffin items. It's a small place, you have to eat standing on high tables where you may rub your back against someone standing behind you. For some who may not able to eat standing, there are about 4 small seats at a folding counter table.
The idlies and Dosa were soft and tasty, the filter coffee was great. Was there for breakfast so couldn't try anything else as we were already full. May be some other time.
Sambar lovers (like me) - they don't serve sambar at all. All items are served with 3 types of chutneys, which are thick with Dosa and little flow with idly. But NO Sambar, at least for now. When I asked the owner why? I was given some reason with an add-on that they may consider adding that in future 🤔
The food items are nice, worth a visit, definitely.

featured_reviews.name: Gaurang Dhamankar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Going to South Bombay for dinner was a disaster. Although the ambience is good, the management is a farce, and the food is quite unhealthy.

Management - The management is very lax. They brought a different dish to our table, claiming that we had ordered it. On resolving the confusion based on bill slips, they asked if we can "adjust" with the different dish instead of them cooking the one we ordered for. The waiters are lax (forgivable), but even the manager is not good at handling crowds during peak hours.

Food - The food was palatable, but it was very oily. I have been to many South Indian restaurants in Thane, but none serve so much oil on the plate. I also felt like trying the hybrid dishes, i.e. modifications of South Indian dishes and I was utterly disappointed with the taste, the filling and obviously, the oil.

Ambience - Ambience is not bad but feels utterly crammed. The tables are not arranged properly, with very little space to move.

Summary - South Indian food is looked at by a perspective of healthy food as an alternative to fast food like pizzas and burgers. Not only does this restaurant break that idea, but it also has very poor management. Ambience is okay, but does not cope up with the negatives. There are much better restaurants for South Indian dishes in town than this one.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Madras Canteen is located in a prime spot, making it easily accessible and perfect for a casual breakfast or an evening snack. The ambiance feels clean and lively, with hygiene being visibly maintained right in front of the customers — a reassuring sign that the food is handled with care.
The service is warm and efficient, ensuring that orders arrive quickly and with a smile. Their paneer masala dosa stands out — crispy on the outside, packed with flavor inside, and perfectly balanced with chutneys. The benne dosa is equally delightful, rich with ghee and cooked just right without any holding back. The rava dosa also deserves mention for its light texture and crispiness, making it a great option for anyone who enjoys a subtler flavor.
Overall, Madras Canteen combines taste, hygiene, and good service into one satisfying dining experience.

featured_reviews.name: Amit Khopade
featured_reviews.review_text:

You could actually see the rava grains standing out on top, almost resembling the coating you get on a rava fish fry rather than a proper dosa. The taste is passable and it definitely lacks any wow factor. It is an okay spot if you just want a decent bite, but do not go in expecting anything extraordinary.
